```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
set.seed(2026)
```

This guide shows a minimal call to `run_scd_analysis()`.

## Data

Use one row per observation, with columns for case, time, phase, and outcome.
The following data are simulated.

```{r}
library(scdbayes)

data <- simulate_scd_data(n_cases = 3, n_phase_a = 5, n_phase_b = 5,
                          effect_size = 1)
head(data[, c("case", "time", "phase", "outcome")], 4)
```

## Fit a model

```{r, eval = FALSE}
result <- run_scd_analysis(data, options = list(family = "gaussian"))
result$diagnostics
```

Model fitting requires Stan and can take time. The result contains the fitted
model, summaries, and diagnostics. Inspect diagnostics before interpreting
results. See `?run_scd_analysis` for arguments.
